```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5)
```

Responsible research assessment, as promoted by DORA and the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment, asks evaluators to recognise the whole range of contributions a researcher makes: software, data, teaching, supervision, transfer, service, open science. academiccareer describes how those contributions develop over a career, from open evidence and from what the researcher declares.

It describes; it does not rank. There is no score, no function to compare people, and no journal-based metric.

```{r setup}
library(academiccareer)
```

## 1. Collect the evidence

`ac_collect()` reads the public records of ORCID, OpenAlex and DataCite for one ORCID iD and merges outputs found in several sources by DOI.

```{r collect, eval = FALSE}
career <- ac_collect("0000-0002-1825-0097", mailto = "you@university.edu")
```

Use it for your own record, or with the person's consent: public records are still personal data. OpenAlex matches works to people automatically and can be wrong, so check the evidence before using it.

This vignette uses the four fictitious careers included in the package (synthetic data), so it needs no network.

```{r example}
career <- ac_example("software")
career
```

## 2. Complete it

Open sources rarely record supervision, teaching, policy advice or outreach. Add them yourself; they are always shown as declared by the researcher.

```{r declare}
career <- ac_add_evidence(career, "supervision_mentoring", "PhD thesis co-supervised",
                          start = 2021, end = 2025, role = "Co-supervisor")
```

Career breaks are part of the context and appear as breaks, not as gaps:

```{r context}
career$context$breaks
```

How well each source covers each dimension matters as much as what it finds:

```{r coverage}
ac_dimensions()[, c("id", "sources", "coverage")]
```

## 3. Timeline

```{r timeline}
tl <- ac_timeline(career)
tl
plot(tl)
```

## 4. Contributions by period and transitions

```{r contributions}
ac_contributions(career)
```

Transitions are found with transparent rules: a new organisation or country, a change in the mix of outputs, the first evidence of a new kind of contribution, a career break.

```{r transitions}
ac_transitions(career)
```

## 5. Profile

The profile highlights what stands out, with documented thresholds, so that careers built on software, data, transfer or teaching become visible.

```{r profile}
ac_profile(career)
```

The four example careers show different profiles:

```{r examples}
for (w in c("traditional", "transfer", "teaching")) {
  cat("\n", w, ":\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste("-", ac_profile(ac_example(w))$statements), sep = "\n")
}
```

Profiles are also available in Spanish:

```{r spanish}
ac_profile(ac_example("teaching"), lang = "es")$statements
```

## 6. Report

```{r report, eval = FALSE}
ac_report(career, "career-report.html")
ac_report(career, "perfil.html", lang = "es")
```
